title: In Vitro Model of Nonreplicating Persistent Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Caseum
author: Xie, Osiecki, et al.
materials: Human monocytic leukemia cell line THP‐1 (ATCC, cat. no. TIB‐202)
Trypan blue solution (0.4%; Gibco, cat. no. 15250061)
T25 (25‐cm2), T75 (75‐cm2), and T175 (175‐cm2) cell culture flasks (Corning, cat. no. 431464U, 430641U, and 431080)
Supplemented RPMI 1640 medium (see recipe) containing 100 µM stearic acid (diluted from 100 mM stearic acid solution; see recipe), 37°C

NOTE: Stearic acid is poorly soluble in aqueous medium. Pre‐warm the RPMI 1640 medium before use to improve solubility. Mix the RPMI medium well by swirling after the addition of 100 µM stearic acid to disperse the whitish precipitate. Any remaining precipitate will dissolve during the overnight incubation at 37°C (see step 1) and will not compromise the experiment.

steps.title: Expand THP-1 cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Culture THP-1 monocytic cells for a total of six weeks in twenty T175 flasks to achieve confluent growth that yields approximately 1 g of caseum surrogate.

substeps.instruction: Add penicillin (100 IU ml⁻¹) and streptomycin (100 µg ml⁻¹) to the medium during the early passages to maintain sterility.
Remove both antibiotics during the final two passages and throughout foam matrix (FM) generation so they do not affect Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) viability or drug tolerance.
If using anhydrotetracycline‑inducible CRISPRi MTB library, employ Tet‑system‑approved (tetracycline‑free) fetal bovine serum throughout THP-1 culture and manipulation.

steps.title: Prepare LD inducer stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make large‑batch stock suspensions of the lipid‑droplet (LD) inducers for consistent use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a γ‑irradiated MTB (iMTB) stock suspension as described in Basic Protocol 1 and aliquot for storage at –20 °C.
Prepare a 100 mM stearic‑acid stock solution (see Alternate Protocol 1) and aliquot for storage at 4 °C.

steps.title: Make stearic‑acid RPMI medium
steps.instruction: Prepare RPMI 1640 medium containing 100 µM stearic acid for fatty‑acid‑induced foam cell generation.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm RPMI 1640 medium to improve stearic‑acid solubility.
Add stearic‑acid stock to the pre‑warmed medium to achieve a final concentration of 100 µM (dilute from the 100 mM stock).
Swirl the mixture well to disperse the whitish precipitate; any remaining precipitate will dissolve during an overnight incubation at 37 °C.

steps.title: Induce lipid droplets in THPMs
steps.instruction: Treat THP‑1‑derived macrophages (THPMs) with an LD inducer to generate foam cells.

substeps.instruction: For the stearic‑acid route, expose THPMs to the 100 µM stearic‑acid‑supplemented RPMI medium for 24 h.
Alternatively, treat THPMs with the iMTB suspension (γ‑irradiated MTB) as an LD inducer; iMTB is BSL‑2‑compatible and retains the ability to modulate macrophage gene expression.

steps.title: Rinse matrix with PBS
steps.instruction: Remove residual RPMI components from the foam matrix by washing.

substeps.instruction: Perform three consecutive rinses of the matrix with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS).

steps.title: Add internal control (optional)
steps.instruction: Introduce an appropriate internal control to the prepared caseum surrogate as needed for downstream assays.

substeps.instruction: Examples include adding moxifloxacin at the desired concentration.
